title: Home
text:
Particle Physics • HERMES • DESY




Explore the proton with real particle-physics data

HERMES Masterclasses is a scientific education site for students, teachers, and physicists. It introduces the HERMES experiment at DESY and prepares learners for guided, simplified analyses inspired by particle-physics measurements.

Start the Masterclass Discover HERMES

title: Mission 1 — Inside the Proton
text:
Mission 01


What does it mean to look inside a proton?
This mission will introduce the idea that protons have internal structure.

title: Mission 1 — Inside the Proton
text:
Goal
Students should build an initial picture of how experiments can probe objects that are too small to see directly.

title: Mission 4 — Spin Mystery
text:
Mission 04


Why is spin a central question in proton structure?
This mission will introduce spin as one of the questions studied in experiments like HERMES.

title: Mission 4 — Spin Mystery
text:
Goal
Students should see that spin is a measurable property, while avoiding unnecessary technical detail at first.

title: Mission 2 — Follow the Quark
text:
Mission 02


How can a measured particle help reconstruct an interaction?
This mission will connect observed particles to the idea of quarks inside a proton.

title: Mission 2 — Follow the Quark
text:
Goal
Students should learn how experimental clues can be used to reason about particle interactions.

title: Mission 3 — Charge and Quark Flavor
text:
Mission 03


What can charge tell us about particle identity?
This mission will focus on electric charge and quark flavor.

title: Mission 3 — Charge and Quark Flavor
text:
Goal
Students should practice linking particle properties to simple classification tasks.

title: About HERMES

Experiment


An introduction to the HERMES experiment at DESY and the questions it helps students explore.

title: About HERMES
text:
Overview
HERMES was an experiment at DESY that investigated the internal structure of matter.
This page will introduce the experiment, the scientific questions it addressed, and why those questions are useful for students learning particle physics.
